audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart contradicted the packet chart and the prose. Rows 2, 3, 4-5 and 6 were wrong in both layers: page said Jax wins Level 2 and 3 while whys[1]/whys[3] describe those as Mordekaiser's windows, and said 'Skill' at Level 6 while whys[4] says Jax flips it.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Skill / Mordekaiser / Skill / Mordekaiser / Jax / Jax / Jax, and it matches the kit: Death's Grasp (E, 16s at rank 1) pulls Jax off the wave so Obliterate lands its isolated-target bonus, and Indestructible absorbs the burst before Counter Strike exists. Jax owns 6+ because Grandmaster's Might's resist burst answers Realm of Death.
audit.corrected: phases[1]/win[1] Mordekaiser, phases[2]/win[2] Skill, phases[3]/win[3] Mordekaiser, phases[4]/win[4] Jax — proposed as matched pairs.

audit.why: Spikes are already right in substance: Morde Lvl 2 (Q+E ranked), Lvl 4-5 shield bully window, Jax Lvl 6 Grandmaster's Might, Jax first item. Only the ultimate's name was wrong.
audit.corrected: Added Realm of Death's real 140/120/100s cooldown to the Level 6 phase why so the bait window is concrete.

audit.whatIsWrong: Jax's ultimate is named 'Grandmaster at Arms' in whys[4], spikes[2].text and mid. Riot's kit file names it Grandmaster's Might (the full layer already uses the correct name, so the page rendered two names for one ability).
audit.why: Fabricated ability name — exactly the calibration error class flagged in the brief. Also the decisive interaction needed stating: Counter Strike dodges basic attacks only, and Mordekaiser's damage is Obliterate + Darkness Rise aura, so E's dodge does far less here than versus an auto-attacker; the stun recast is the value, and Indestructible can absorb it.
audit.corrected: Grandmaster's Might everywhere; Level 3 phase why now states the auto-dodge-vs-ability-damage interaction and the recast requirement.

audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 4-5 phase why gave no cooldown anchor.
audit.why: Counter Strike is 17/15/13/11/9s; at rank 3 (levels 4-5) it is 13s down, which is the actual reason Morde bullies that window.
audit.corrected: Phase 3 why now names the 13s gap.

edits.before: Counter Strike flips every AA exchange he starts. Only take the trade when Mordekaiser's Realm of Death is down.
edits.after: Death's Grasp drags you off the wave so Obliterate lands its isolated bonus, and you have no Counter Strike yet to answer.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Mordekaiser must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Counter Strike is online but his damage is Obliterate, not autos — trade only when you can recast the stun, or Indestructible eats it.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Realm of Death's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: His bully window: Indestructible tanks your stun while Counter Strike sits down 13s at rank 3, so give ground unless you can land the recast.

edits.before: Grandmaster’s Might stats win every extended duel from here on. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Mordekaiser's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Grandmaster's Might flips it — bait Realm of Death (140s at rank 1) and pop the active's Armor and MR as the realm lands to win his forced 1v1.

edits.before: Grandmaster at Arms flips it — bait Realm of Death, then the active's burst of Armor and MR lets you survive the steal while your Relentless Assault ramps and out-damages him in the 1v1 he forced.
edits.after: Grandmaster's Might flips it — bait Realm of Death, then the active's burst of Armor and MR lets you survive the steal while your Relentless Assault ramps and out-damages him in the 1v1 he forced.

edits.before: Grandmaster at Arms flips the duel: pop the active Armor/MR the instant Realm of Death pulls you in, and the burst of resists plus your every-third-hit on-hit ramp lets you out-damage him inside his own 1v1 and win the forced fight.
edits.after: Grandmaster's Might flips the duel: pop the active Armor/MR the instant Realm of Death pulls you in, and the burst of resists plus your every-third-hit on-hit ramp lets you out-damage him inside his own 1v1 and win the forced fight.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are still his — his W shield eats the Counter Strike stun and he keeps slamming while your E is down, so only trade when you can recast the stun, never when he can just shield it. Then 6 is your flip: he WILL eventually press Realm of Death to drag you into the 1v1 and steal your stats, so bait it, and the moment the realm closes pop Grandmaster at Arms's active for the burst of Armor and MR — those resists, not the on-hit, are what let you tank his isolated Q while your Relentless Assault ramps and kills him. Keep the wave pulled near you so when he walks up to slam he's already inside Leap Strike range for the re-engage.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are still his — Indestructible eats the Counter Strike stun and he keeps slamming while your E is down 13s, so only trade when you can recast the stun, never when he can just shield it. Then 6 is your flip: he WILL eventually press Realm of Death to drag you into the 1v1 and steal your stats, so bait it, and the moment the realm closes pop Grandmaster's Might for its burst of Armor and MR — those resists, not the on-hit, are what let you tank his isolated Obliterate while Relentless Assault ramps and kills him. Keep the wave pulled near you so when he walks up to slam he's already inside Leap Strike range for the re-engage.

notes: Jax's R was written as 'Grandmaster at Arms' in three content-layer fields while the full layer used the correct 'Grandmaster's Might' — the page showed two names for one ability. Packet suspectNames were all false positives (Counter Strike, Realm of Death, Leap Strike are the real names); the genuine error was the one the suspect scan missed.
